# Shellbell

> Shellbell is a private, self-hosted terminal notification system. It sends Web Push notifications when long-running terminal work is ready for attention without collecting command text, command output, exit codes, environment variables, working directories, process lists, or inferred outcomes.

Shellbell is open-source software for Linux x86-64, Linux ARM64, Raspberry Pi OS, and WSL 2. It supports opt-in monitoring for Bash, Zsh, and Fish, manual notifications, a durable local queue, a private relay, an installable PWA, and tagged notification receivers.

## Primary resources

- [Guided installation and self-hosting](https://kinghacker9000.github.io/shellbell/): Mobile-friendly setup for the CLI, pairing, receivers, validation, and owning the relay.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/KingHacker9000/shellbell): Canonical source code, issues, pull requests, and project history.
- [README](https://github.com/KingHacker9000/shellbell/blob/main/README.md): Product overview, quick start, commands, supported environments, and documentation map.
- [Latest release](https://github.com/KingHacker9000/shellbell/releases/latest): Verified Linux x86-64 and ARM64 archives, installer, checksums, and container image details.
- [Full AI context](https://kinghacker9000.github.io/shellbell/llms-full.txt): Consolidated machine-readable description, setup, architecture, privacy boundaries, and usage.

## Canonical facts

- Stable release: v0.1.1
- License: MIT
- Relay model: private, single-owner, self-hosted
- Client platforms: Linux x86-64, Linux ARM64, Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit, WSL 2
- Shells: Bash, Zsh, Fish
- Delivery: Web Push to tagged browser receivers
- Privacy boundary: shell activity timing and state transitions, not shell contents
